decision: Accept the originating spec's four-axis model (operator_surface x agent_runtime x role x execution_locality) as the frame, but reject its literal seven-feature decomposition where it duplicates existing subsystems. agent_runtime (agent_surface.py + executors/AGENT_REGISTRY + KNOWN_OPERATOR_AGENTS) and role (roles CLI + agent register-worker + role_assignment.py) and execution_locality (environments.json + worktree + DispatchTask.cwd) already exist. The only fully-absent axis is operator_surface.
rationale: DontPanic governance avoids parallel/competing registries. The genuinely-new work is the operator_surface axis, detection, a presence ledger, easy role choice, a channel doctor, and a dashboard render.

decision: REVISED per operator critique: operator-role choice is SETTABLE in v0 (F004), not deferred. It is a layer separate from the worker-dispatch ROLES (implementer/auditor/goal_auditor), stored under a distinct operator_roles.* config namespace, with NO assert_registrable guard so non-executor surfaces (e.g. cursor) can be assigned. The existing roles / agent register-worker worker paths are untouched. Easy set/list CLI + dashboard role-matrix projection deliver the 'Claude primary, Codex auditor, Gemini researcher' UX that was the core of the ask.
rationale: The first draft deferred settable operator roles, missing the explicit product requirement (easy role choice). Conflating the two role namespaces would break the executor guard, so they stay separate but both are first-class in v0.

decision: Forbid a new agent-channels.json registry. The channel/role view (F006) is derived at build time from the invocation ledger + executors/AGENT_REGISTRY + capabilities/*.json (incl. the new operator-surface manifests from F005) + worktree bindings + operator_roles. A test asserts no agent-channels.json is introduced.
rationale: A hand-maintained channel registry would drift from the executor registry and capability manifests that already encode the same facts.

decision: REVISED scope: defer ONLY the fully-open adapter marketplace (third-party adapter submission/registry format) and remote-locality enforcement/routing. doctor --channel (F005) and settable operator roles (F004) are pulled INTO v0 per the critique.
rationale: Those two were the practical heart of the ask ('will this work from Cursor/Codex/Antigravity?' and 'make role choice easy'); deferring them left the plan architecturally sound but product-thin. The marketplace and remote enforcement remain genuinely demand-gated.

decision: The presence ledger (F003) must be concurrency- and privacy-hardened: atomic/lock-safe append under multiple simultaneous agents, command-string argument redaction (tokens/secrets in args, beyond field-name checks), no raw home paths (sanitized like audit evidence), and a retention/compaction policy.
rationale: Multiple agents run at once; a naive append corrupts under concurrency, and command strings can carry tokens in arguments. The audit-evidence-writer-hygiene work (PR #48) is the precedent for path/identity sanitization.

decision: execution_locality is a sharp enum (local_mac, plan_worktree, dashboard_terminal, remote_vm, code_task, unknown), not a thin local|remote.
rationale: The Cowork-VM-vs-Mac-code-task distinction is the reason the axis exists; local|remote cannot represent worktree vs dashboard-terminal vs code-task localities or drive the remote_cannot_mutate_local conflict semantics.

decision: Operator surfaces/runtimes that are not executors (Cursor, Antigravity, Claude Desktop, Codex app) get capability-manifest shape via a new operator_surface kind in the EXISTING capability schema (F005), with seeded manifests — NOT a new registry. This is what makes 'derive from capabilities' real for surfaces that have no executor.
rationale: The first draft named these surfaces in the enum but derived support only from executors/capabilities, which many surfaces lack. Extending the capability manifest shape closes that gap while honoring the no-new-registry decision.

decision: F006's dashboard conflict/health semantics go beyond same_plan_conflict to include same_branch, same_repo, unhealthy_worktree_binding, remote_cannot_mutate_local, and operator_only_runtime_not_dispatchable, derived by joining the ledger with worktree bindings and agent_surface dispatchability.
rationale: Same-plan conflict alone misses the real collision and health cases operators hit when multiple agents share branches/worktrees or when an operator-only runtime cannot be dispatched.
